case_name: Sanghi Brothers (Indore) Pvt. Ltd. v Sanjay Choudhary And Ors.
facts: The appellant-company is a registered company dealing with the sale of auto vehicles at Indore and respondents are Directors of the Chetak Construction Ltd.
In the year 1988-89 accused approached the complainant company for obtaining lease of Tata dumpers and light commercial vehicles for a specific period on monthly lease rent basis.
Agreements were executed between the parties on 13.5.1988, 14.11.1988 and 25.3.1989 for delivery of 25 dumpers, 10 dumpers, 20 dumpers and 4 light commercial vehicles
After some time, complainant came to know that accused No.4 was unable to pay him lease rent according to the agreement.

Complainant called accused No.1 and 2 to execute personal guarantee bonds in favour of the complainant and after some persuasion, so called personal guarantee bonds were executed by the accused Nos. 1 and 2 in favour of the complainant for due performance of the agreement on 6.12.1991.
issues: Whether the framing of charge was sustainable?
petitioner_arguments: The conclusions of the High Court are clearly indefensible.
It is not a requirement of law that the offence is not so unimpeachable and if it is not rebutted, conviction can be based on it.
There must be some mental evil design to constitute fraud.
The intention was very clear, because it was aimed at preventing the appellant from exercising the right of re-possession.
respondent_arguments: The background facts have been rightly taken note of by the High Court to conclude that the framing of charge was not sustainable.
There was no intention of committing the alleged fraud as has been rightly held by the High Court.
Even if it is conceded that there was breach of contract at some point of time that was remedied because of the permission to sell vehicles and by encashment of the bank guarantee.
court_reasoning: If on the basis of materials on record, a court could come to the conclusion that commission of the offence is a probable consequence; a case for framing of charge exists.
At the stage of framing of a charge, probative value of the materials on record cannot be gone into; the materials brought on record by the prosecution has to be accepted as true at that stage.
The Court has to see while considering the question of framing the charge as to whether the material brought on record could reasonably connect the accused with the trial.
holding: The appeal is allowed. Appeal allowed
cases_cited: In State of Maharashtra and Ors. V. Som Nath Thapa
Sanghi Brothers (Indore) Pvt. Ltd. v Sanjay Choudhary
and State of West Bengal v. Mohd
